evidence.what: Rug edge is a rounded rollover with visible serged-binding ribs (repeating light stitch lumps along the lip) and a soft contact shadow on the wood under the lip; the corner is radiused, not a razor 90-degree step.

Field texture at 100%: directional abrasion streaks with lighter slub flecks running one weave direction - reads as a vintage-washed short-pile/viscose product, not isotropic noise; motif patches ~100-300 mm at this footprint, plausible for a ~2.4x3.0 m rug, no visible tiling repeat.
Contact shadow pools under the bench base and the rug texture continues into the darkened zone - the bench sits ON the rug and the rug sits ON the floor; no float gap.

In the eye frame the bed-skirt corner casts a soft diagonal shadow ON the rug and the distressed streak texture stays continuous through the shadow - grounding evidence that the rug is a lit surface lying flat, not a pasted stain plane.

note: Judged from pixels only, blind to build history. The rug reads as a credible purchased product: distressed vintage-wash field with directional grain, serged rollover binding, radiused corner, and contact shadows in both frames. Weakest area: the eye frame's far rug-to-wood boundary near (2235,1565) is soft (distance/DOF) - the thickness lip is faint there, but it is a soft transition, not a knife edge, and the wardrobe frame shows the same edge treatment sharply. Whether the rug is beautiful remains the owner's call; this verdict covers credibility only.
